Diorama 0.9.0 brings back the old fog, and adds a shared map and a web map for servers.

### Changed

- The fog over unexplored land is the soft fog from before 0.8.0 again. The clouds are gone, so nothing covers land you've already explored.

### New

- Shared map: put Diorama on a dedicated server and every player with Diorama sees the land anyone has explored, drawn with their own resource pack. It's on as soon as the jar is in the server's `mods` folder (`share-map` in `config/diorama-server.properties` turns it off). Overworld and End; the Nether stays your own.
- Web map: a server with Diorama can show its map in a browser, no mod needed. Set `web-map=true` in `config/diorama-server.properties`, restart, and open port 8100.
- Nether portals built on the Nether roof get their own pin.

Players without Diorama can still join a server that has it, and Diorama players can join servers without it.

updates.changelog:
# Olaf's Relatively Placed Blocks 2.0.2

A patch for 2.0.1, for every supported version (1.20.1, 1.21.1, 1.21.5, 1.21.8, 1.21.10, 1.21.11, 26.1, 26.2 and 26.3). Thanks to everyone who sent reports and logs!

## Fixes
- **1.21.10 and 1.21.11: shared spaces now redraw at once.**
  - Placing a block into a shared space, or breaking one out of it, didn't show until another block was placed next to it. The client was told about the change but never asked to redraw the chunk. It is now, the same as on the other versions.

## New
- **A config file to keep specific blocks out:** `config/relativeblocks.json`, written on first launch.
  - `never_share` lists blocks that may never share a space, by relative placement or as a mixed slab. It is read again on `/reload`.
  - `no_orthostats` lists slabs that get no orthostat (vertical slab). It takes effect on the next game start.
  - Entries are block ids in four forms: one block (`minecraft:rail`), a whole mod (`somemod:*`), a pattern (`*:*_fence`), or, for `never_share` only, a block tag (`#minecraft:flowers`).
  - Everything not listed still works exactly as before; the lists only take blocks out. A bad entry is reported in the log and skipped, never a crash.

## Changes
- **Blocks that fill their space no longer share it.**
  - Some blocks have no collision box but still take up their whole block, and the mod was letting them share a space as if they were flowers. That is fixed for snow layers, fire, rails, cobwebs, powder snow, string (tripwire), frogspawn, redstone dust, nether portals, vines, glow lichen, sculk veins, resin clumps, kelp, big dripleaf, and two-block plants such as tall grass, large ferns, sunflowers, lilacs, rose bushes, peonies and pitcher plants. The 1.21.5+ bushes (bush, firefly bush) are included as well, since their hit box is the full block.
  - **Crops** (wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroots, nether wart, torchflower and pitcher crops, pumpkin and melon stems, sweet berry bushes, cave vines, weeping and twisting vines, mangrove propagules) and **flowerbeds** (pink petals, wildflowers, leaf litter) no longer share either: they grow or spread to fill their own patch.
  - **Invisible technical blocks** such as the structure void are left alone.
  - All of this is decided by the block's shape and properties, not by a list of names, so other mods' blocks of the same kind behave the same way.
  - Still shareable as before: flowers, short grass, ferns, dead bushes, saplings, mushrooms, fungi, roots, sea pickles, seagrass, cactus flowers, torches, levers, buttons, bamboo, cocoa, flower pots, candles, lanterns, chains, end rods, lightning rods, fences, panes, bars, walls and gates.
- **For pack makers:** redstone dust has left the `relativeblocks:relative_placement_denied` tag, since the shape rule now covers it. Pressure plates and sugar cane remain in it.

## Good to know
- Blocks that stop sharing in this patch are only kept from being placed together from now on. Anything already sharing a space in your world stays as it is.
- Removing the mod from a world that already has orthostats or shared blocks in it shows a "Missing content" warning. Back up your world before removing any mod that adds blocks.

updates.name: Punchy!
updates.changelog:
# Punchy v3.2

## New

- Punchy now steps aside while another mod draws your hands in first person, and takes over again when it's done:
  - Spell casting in Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks
  - Epic Fight's battle mode
  - Mowzie's Mobs' abilities, such as the Sun's Blessing
  - Carrying a block or an animal with Carry On
  - Looking through another entity, when a mod moves your first-person camera to it
  - Better Combat's first-person attacks, when you turn Better Combat Support off. It's on by default, which keeps Punchy's arms and plays Punchy's own attacks instead.
- Guns and gadgets that bring their own first-person model now show it, hands included: Timeless and Classics Zero and Create's potato cannon.
- Modded fire now shows its own look on your burning arms, such as the blue soul fire of Soul Fire'd.
- New setting, Show Both Hands (General): your empty off hand shows next to the other one, so you see both hands when you hold nothing in it.
- New setting, Built-in Mod Support (Compatibility): Punchy's own support for the mods above. It's on by default; turn it off to see a mod without Punchy's help. Better Combat Support is a separate switch.
- Smarter boat rowing, now also on 1.20.1, 1.21.1 and 1.21.5:
  - The paddles sit in your hands and move with them as you row.
  - A hand that holds an item keeps it, and the other hand rows on its own. With both hands busy, nobody rows.
  - A shield stays on your arm, so that hand still rows.
  - A paddle no hand holds rests in its oarlock instead of disappearing.
  - Turning pulls one paddle, the way the boat itself does, and rowing back has its own stroke.
  - Holding something with both hands, the empty hand lets go to row and comes back when you stop.
  - The paddles in your hands match your boat's wood and a raft's bamboo.

## Changes

- The Compatibility options for Interactive Stuff, Better Combat and Sword Blocking Mechanics are now on by default, and turned on once for existing settings. Interactive Stuff's and Sword Blocking Mechanics' options only act while their mod is installed, and Better Combat Support acts while Better Combat or Spell Engine is installed.
- The Punchy menu now opens on General the first time, and General is the first tab.
- Mix Packs is easier to use. Pointing at an item previews it, and the preview stays on it while you reach for the preview's arrows. Click an item to see its packs, point at a pack to try it in the preview, and click one to use it. Every pick can be undone from the message it shows.
- Mix Packs setups: Current choices is now called No setup, and Use resource pack order is now Reset to pack order.

## Fixes

- 26.3 and 26.4: the new explorer maps, such as the Dappled Forest camp maps and the village, temple and treasure maps, are now held like a regular map instead of behind your forearm.
- Armor on your arms now uses the texture a mod gives its armor, so Create's copper backtank no longer turns your arm dark (NeoForge 1.21.1).
- Create's netherite backtank now shows its dark diving suit sleeve on your arms in first person, as it does without Punchy (Forge 1.20.1 and NeoForge 1.21.1).
- Your arms no longer show while you're invisible, as in vanilla. Held items still show.
- Crossbows with Quick Charge now play their charge animation faster.
- The brush is now left to Minecraft, so its brushing motion shows again, unless a resource pack animates the brush.
- Armor with its own model now shows its real sleeve on your arms instead of a black one, such as Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks and Mowzie's Mobs (Forge 1.20.1 and NeoForge 1.21.1), and L_Ender's Cataclysm and Alex's Caves (Forge 1.20.1).
- The Aether's gloves stay on your arms as they move, also on a hand holding an item (Forge 1.20.1).
- A raised shield no longer turns oddly in one hand after you change resource packs (1.21.11 and newer).
- NeoForge 26.2: the game no longer opens a warning screen about Punchy's icon at every launch.
- Forge 1.21.1 and newer: camera animations now turn the view. Before, only their moves showed.
- Forge 1.21.5: Punchy's keys are back, such as F8 for the menu and the inspect key, and Punchy reads resource packs again when they reload.
- Forge 26.1 and newer: Punchy can now tell which mods are installed, which its built-in mod support and a pack's `requires_mods` depend on.
- Mix Packs: a pick now takes effect right away on 1.20.1 and 1.21.1, without restarting the game.
- Mix Packs: a pick made while a setup is loaded no longer goes back at the next start.
- Mix Packs: the Mace row shows an iron axe on 1.20.1, which has no mace, instead of nothing.
- Glowing armor keeps its glow on your arms with a shader pack, such as the armor of T.O Magic 'n Extras (Forge 1.20.1).

## Performance

- Items with model parts are much lighter to draw, most of all ones with long animations. A heavy item now allocates about two thirds less memory per frame (measured on 26.3).
- 26.2 and newer: without Iris, Punchy no longer looks for Iris's classes again in every frame, for every item you hold.

## For mod makers

- Everything below is documented on the wiki: https://wiki.punchymod.com/punchy/api
- Punchy API version 3: a mod can tell Punchy what happens in it (its own moments and states, facts about its items), ask what Punchy shows (who draws each hand, which clip plays, the clips the packs have), hear Punchy's clips, moments, reloads and settings changes, and play or steer the clips resource packs ship. It can also change how Punchy reads its items: their kind, role, pose, equips and swings, and how the off arm shows. Animation stays the packs' job: no call hands Punchy a clip or a canned motion.
- Every registration has an id and a priority, can be taken back, and shows in Copy debug info with its cost. Players can turn off a mod's calls in Compatibility; its rule files and rules from code stay.
- Also new since 3.1: `leaveBothHandsToMinecraft`, `leaveHandsToMinecraft`, `hideArms`, `hideArmorOnArms`, `flames` and `version()`, all general calls that any mod can use for its own case.
- `leaveItemsToMinecraft` now works everywhere Punchy's own item blacklist does: drawing, animations, the equip motion and item model properties.
- What an arm is drawn with: `armTexture` gives an arm another texture, tint or light, `armOverlays` adds layers over the skin, `armFlames` lights flames without fire, and `hideLayers` hides single layers, such as the skin, the sleeve or the held item.
- `drawOnArm` is an arm event on every loader, Fabric included, on Punchy's animated arm. `drawItem` takes over or decorates the draw of a held item at Punchy's grip. `handPointInWorld` and `handPointOnScreen` say where a point on the hand or the item appears.
- `movementScale` scales Punchy's sway by channel, `itemDisplay` picks a held item's display context, and `keepItemUseVisuals` keeps an item model's own use look.
- `restrictSetting` turns a feature off for a while without saving it, `menuRows` adds a mod's rows to Punchy's tabs, and `editorTarget` adds a mod's target to the Hand Editor, saved with the profile.

## For pack creators

- Rule files and the rest of this section on the wiki: https://wiki.punchymod.com/punchy/api#rule-files-for-packs-and-mod-jars
- Rule files: a resource pack or a mod jar can ship `assets/<namespace>/punchy_rules/*.json` to leave items to Minecraft, by item id, namespace, tag or class, with no code. They can also set item kinds and roles, skip equips, hold clips back, define conditions and moments, add camera kicks to moments and turn off one of Punchy's own mod supports, and most entries can be limited to when their conditions, held or worn items and installed mods say.
- Compat entries can play a clip on a moment, Punchy's own or a mod's, and every entry takes `when`, `unless` and `requires_mods`.
- First-person and item model clips can read numbers in their keyframes, such as `q.health_fraction` or a mod's `v.<mod>.<name>`. Don't write these in third-person clips, which read numbers only.
- First-person clips can set their own `speed`, `blend_in` and `aliases`, `sound_effects` can play any sound event with its own volume and pitch, and a timeline token with a namespace is a marker that fires a moment.
- A model parts item can play a clip on a moment (`on:<moment>`) or hold one while a condition is true (`while:<condition>`) in `modelPartsAnimation`, and a particle's `on_animation` can name a moment, written `<moment>@0`.
- A pack can show the player one card with the settings it plays best with and the mods it needs or clashes with. Nothing changes until the player says so.
- Rule files can give an arm another texture, tint or light (`arm_texture`), add layers that fade in and out (`arm_overlays`), light flames without fire (`arm_flames`), hide single layers, pick a held item's display context (`display_context`) and keep an item's own use look (`keep_use_visuals`).
- Compat entries can change an item's and an arm's pose while conditions hold (`poses`), eased over a time you set.
- A pack can offer named setups of settings, hand poses and Mix Packs choices: `assets/<namespace>/punchy/presets/*.json`. They show in Profiles in the F8 menu.

updates.name: Diorama
updates.changelog:
Diorama 0.8.0 brings night to the map, covers unexplored land with Minecraft's own clouds, and lets you turn the map to face any side. Create's trains and contraptions now show on the map too.

### New

- **Night on the map.** The map and minimap get dark at night like the world does, and torches, lamps and lava light them up. Storms darken it too. Pick **Day and night** on the Look tab: World time, Always day or Always night. World time is the default. Caves and the Nether don't change. Image export has a **Night** box. Maps from older versions get their lights as they're drawn again: in singleplayer that happens by itself from the save, and on servers as you revisit places.
- **Clouds over unexplored land.** The fog of war is now Minecraft's own blocky clouds, taken from the game's cloud texture, or from your resource pack if it has its own. They're solid over land you've never seen and thin out to see-through near land you have. Zoomed out, the cloud blocks grow so they stay about the same size on screen. They draw faster than the old fog, and they no longer flicker after you turn the map. Caves and the Nether keep the old fog.
- **Turn the map.** A compass button on the map screen turns the map to face north, east, south or west, so you can see the front of builds that don't face south. Shift turns it the other way. Each world remembers its direction, and the minimap follows. While a side is redrawn, the old map stays visible under the clouds, and the spot you're looking at is drawn first. On servers, walk around to map a new side.
- **Create contraptions on the map.** Trains, windmills, bearings, pistons and other moving Create builds draw on the map and minimap in 3D, with shadows, and move as they do in the world (thanks to LegendarySpy).
- **The surface view stays on under a roof.** Inside a house the minimap no longer switches to the cave view; it waits until you're really below ground. It's the new **Prefer the surface** setting on the Minimap tab, on by default. With the map open, it now follows you between the surface and caves, until you pick a layer yourself (thanks to TaCraft-Sociality).
- **Steadier cave view, and Legible cave maps.** Jumping no longer flips the cave minimap to another slice, and when it does change it fades over. The new **Legible cave maps** setting on the Minimap tab shades caves by depth. It's off by default, as in Xaero's. Ground further below you fades to dark slate, and the map shows your own cave instead of seeing through the rock (thanks to LegendarySpy).
- **Water shows its depth.** Deep water is darker than shallow water, sandy shallows turn turquoise, and the seafloor's outlines fade out a few blocks down (thanks to LegendarySpy).
- **Portal pins.** Turn on **Portal pins** on the Waypoints tab to get a pin on every lit Nether portal, End portal and End gateway the map finds. Off by default.
- **The minimap zooms further out.** Four more steps, down to 0.1875×, which shows 512 blocks across at the default size.
- **Sharper when zoomed out.** Zoomed out, the map was soft. Each screen pixel now shows the average of the land under it. Full zoom looks the same as before.
- **No fog while zooming.** Zooming the full map, even a quick scroll, keeps the ground on screen while the new zoom level loads, instead of showing fog (thanks to faceincase).
- **Xaero's Minimap import is easier to find.** With Xaero's installed, its U key opens Xaero's own list, so Diorama's import button stayed hidden. Now, if Xaero's has waypoints for the world that Diorama doesn't, a chat line a few seconds after joining has an **[Import]** link.
- Russian and Belarusian translations are up to date (thanks to Gazmanovich).

### Fixed

- Grass, leaves and water at the edge of your view distance came out in Plains colours, which left a coloured strip round the loaded area and thin lines across server maps. They now get the right colour.
- On 26.x, the game could crash at night with the map showing when a lit spot lost its last light, for example when you broke the only torch nearby.
- Panning with the middle mouse button while measuring froze the measuring tool. It now keeps following the cursor.
- Holding Shift with the line or area tool now keeps the line due north, south, east or west on the ground. Before, it stayed level on screen, so on a slope it drifted south.
- Leaving and quickly coming back to a world while the map filled in from the save could mix up the fill's progress.
- The map's tooltip said Plains everywhere outside the loaded area. It now shows no biome where the game doesn't know it.
- While spectating through another player, your arrow and coordinates now move with them instead of staying where you started watching.
- On some servers new builds never showed on the map, even after rejoining. They do now.
- GPU drawing could turn itself off for good after its first-start check in big build worlds, leaving the map on the slower processor drawing. Water and shadow edges now match, one unlucky check gets a second try, and if it turned off for you in 0.7.0 it checks again once on 0.8.0.
- If the graphics driver crashes the game during the first GPU drawing of a cave, the next start draws on the processor instead of crashing again.
- The waypoint editor's preview shows the ground at the waypoint, in its own dimension, instead of where you're standing.
- Bed, death and portal pins show their names in your language, and follow you if you switch.
- Block colours are averaged the way the eye sees them, so a block with a bright frame and a dark middle, like Create's railway casing, no longer comes out too light.

### Faster

- Flying over new land no longer freezes the game now and then to clean up memory, and the slowest frames while flying are shorter.
- New land fills in about 20% faster.
- The radar and the map screen's toolbar take less time each frame.

updates.name: Punchy!
updates.changelog:
# Punchy v3.2a

A hotfix for 3.2.

## Fixes

- Punchy's built-in animations move more smoothly: every clip of the built-in pack eases in and out of its poses, while fast moves such as punches and swings keep their snap.
- Rowing a boat in first person is rebuilt, instead of sweeping the paddles flat across the view like a swimming stroke:
  - Your arms row one continuous stroke. Starting, stopping, turning and backing up ease into it and out of it, so nothing ever snaps or restarts, even when you steer with short taps.
  - The stroke keeps time with the boat's own paddles, one stroke for each splash, and answers your keys at once. Backing up rows slowly and gently, since a boat backs up slowly.
  - Each hand holds its oar by the end of the handle, at the side of your fist, and the oar runs out of your hand toward the water without ever twisting. The oars stay outside the boat: their blades dip into the water beside it as they pull, come back above it, and never show through the hull, wherever you look.
  - Looking down at the boat brings your rowing arms up into view; looking up lets them drop away.
  - Your body faces the boat while you look around: your rowing arms and their oars stay with the boat, so looking to a side shows the arm on that side reaching for its oar.
  - Turning while both hands are on their oars rows one side: that arm reaches further and pulls longer, your body leans into it a little, and the other arm rests.
  - An empty hand, or a hand with a shield on its forearm, holds its oar for the whole ride. A hand that holds anything else keeps it, and everything it does, while the other hand rows.
  - When both hands hold items, your off hand puts its item away as soon as you row and takes it out again once the boat settles, so a rower always shows and your main hand stays ready.
  - Punching, using an item or switching items lets that hand go of its oar at once, and it takes the oar back after; the other hand keeps rowing.
  - A hand that takes or lets go of its oar moves there smoothly, or dips out of view and comes back up with its oar or its item, the way Minecraft lowers and raises a held item.
  - You can attack and use items while you row: Minecraft no longer counts your hands as busy on the paddles while Punchy's boat animations are on.
- A resource pack's own model for a held chest now shows, instead of Punchy's built-in chest drawn huge in front of the view. The same goes for boats, rafts, minecarts, the enchanting table and pistons.
- Switching to another hotbar slot in the middle of a long animation, such as lighting a fire with flint and steel, now ends it right away, also when a resource pack has no switch animation for the new item, such as an empty hand.
- The brush is held in Punchy's hand again. While you brush, Minecraft's brushing motion shows, unless a resource pack animates the brush.
- With Create, the extendo grip in your off hand no longer shows a second arm holding your main-hand item next to the grip.
- With Epic Fight, Punchy no longer draws your hands in battle mode while you hold a map.
- On 1.20.1 and 1.21.1, the glowing parts of resource pack item models, such as a torch's flame, are no longer burned out to white, and the parts around them keep their colors.
- With Entity Model Features and a resource pack that animates the player in first person, the arm no longer swings far too much while you wear Create's netherite backtank.
- With GeckoLib installed, item models from resource packs whose textures animate, such as a fancy water bucket, show again instead of a grey box.
- With ReArm, mining with an axe no longer makes the arm shake and skip its animation. An axe that a mod lets you throw is held like a spear only while you charge the throw.

## For pack creators

- Rowing with the oars in first person plays new clips of the built-in pack, `oar_row`, `oar_row_back`, `oar_row_left`, `oar_row_right` and `oar_rest`, so a pack can change the stroke like any other clip. `oar_row_left` and `oar_row_right` are one arm rowing alone, for turns with both hands on their oars; a pack without them rows one arm with `oar_row`. The older `rowing` and `rowing_back` clips no longer play in first person.
- `oar_rest` can carry an `oar` object that places the oar in the hand: `rest` (the oar at rest) and `stroke` (the oar at points of the forward stroke, 0 to 1), each six numbers, a turn in degrees and a move in pixels in the arm's own frame, and `thickness`. Rowing back runs the stroke backwards, and the left oar mirrors the right. The paddle in the hand follows it instead of the paddle tuning. A pack without placements can still set `pivot` and `grip`, and its oars then run from the fist through the pivot. Either way, Punchy turns an oar that would show through the boat out of it.
- `disable_arm_tuning` now works on clips of the overlay layer, such as rowing and swimming, as it does on other clips. The oar clips use it, so their keys are the whole arm pose whatever the hand holds.
- A pack's model parts definition for an item now wins over Punchy's own in-hand models of chests, boats, minecarts, the enchanting table and pistons.
- New: model parts definitions can have `variants`, which give the same item other models or textures by what the held stack holds: the potion of a potion, splash potion, lingering potion or tipped arrow, and whether a crossbow is loaded, and with what. Each variant has a `when` with `potion` or `charged`, and the fields it changes.

# Shiroi Visuals Rework

In this version, we've reworked several rendering systems to improve the overall visual quality, lighting accuracy, and atmosphere of the Overworld.

These changes include improvements to atmospheric rendering, shadow precision, color reproduction, and ambient bloom. We've also introduced a series of optimizations to reduce rendering overhead and improve overall performance.

Additionally, this update introduces **Vivid Lamps**, an optional advanced lighting system that allows light-emitting blocks to illuminate their surroundings and cast dynamic shadows in real time.

**Note:** Vivid Lamps can significantly increase GPU usage, particularly when multiple light sources are visible. For this reason, the feature is disabled by default.

![Jungle forest](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/dfa971b4c396f1cfee39dea97715843ad445f46a.png)

## Changelog:

### Looks

- Completely reworked atmospheric rendering to improve the overall appearance and consistency of the Overworld.
- Reworked environmental lighting for more vibrant and natural illumination.
- Improved shadow precision and consistency across different lighting conditions.
- Adjusted color reproduction for more accurate and balanced tones while preserving the original Vanilla appearance.
- Reworked ambient bloom to improve light diffusion and reduce excessive brightness around illuminated surfaces.

### New Features

**Vivid Lamps**

- Added an optional real-time lighting system for torches, lanterns, and other light-emitting blocks.
- Light sources can now illuminate nearby surfaces dynamically.
- Added support for dynamic shadows cast by supported light sources.
- Introduced multiple lighting modes to balance visual quality and performance.

![Vivid Lamps turn on!](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/c3e2a5abc1b4b23161b844353ff11ce94eccca91.png)

**Available Modes:**

- **OFF (Default):** Disables Vivid Lamps entirely.
- **BOOST:** Enables enhanced real-time lighting without dynamic shadows.
- **ON:** Enables real-time lighting with dynamic shadow casting.

### Improvements

- Refined lighting calculations to improve transitions between illuminated and unlit areas.
- Improved overall visual consistency between atmospheric lighting, shadows, and environmental colors.
- Adjusted bloom behavior to better integrate with the updated lighting system.

### Performance

- Introduced several rendering optimizations to reduce GPU overhead.
- Optimized various shader calculations to improve performance without compromising visual quality.
- Vivid Lamps remains disabled by default due to the additional rendering cost of dynamic lighting and shadow generation.

**Note:** Performance improvements may vary depending on hardware, resolution, and enabled graphical features. Vivid Lamps, particularly in ON mode, may have a significant performance impact in environments containing multiple light sources.

Diorama 0.9.0 brings back the old fog, and adds a shared map and a web map for servers.

### Changed

- The fog over unexplored land is the soft fog from before 0.8.0 again. The clouds are gone, so nothing covers land you've already explored.

### New

- Shared map: put Diorama on a dedicated server and every player with Diorama sees the land anyone has explored, drawn with their own resource pack. It's on as soon as the jar is in the server's `mods` folder (`share-map` in `config/diorama-server.properties` turns it off). Overworld and End; the Nether stays your own.
- Web map: a server with Diorama can show its map in a browser, no mod needed. Set `web-map=true` in `config/diorama-server.properties`, restart, and open port 8100.
- Nether portals built on the Nether roof get their own pin.

Players without Diorama can still join a server that has it, and Diorama players can join servers without it.

updates.name: Olafs Relatively Placed Blocks
updates.changelog:
# Olaf's Relatively Placed Blocks 2.0.2

A patch for 2.0.1, for every supported version (1.20.1, 1.21.1, 1.21.5, 1.21.8, 1.21.10, 1.21.11, 26.1, 26.2 and 26.3). Thanks to everyone who sent reports and logs!

## Fixes
- **1.21.10 and 1.21.11: shared spaces now redraw at once.**
  - Placing a block into a shared space, or breaking one out of it, didn't show until another block was placed next to it. The client was told about the change but never asked to redraw the chunk. It is now, the same as on the other versions.

## New
- **A config file to keep specific blocks out:** `config/relativeblocks.json`, written on first launch.
  - `never_share` lists blocks that may never share a space, by relative placement or as a mixed slab. It is read again on `/reload`.
  - `no_orthostats` lists slabs that get no orthostat (vertical slab). It takes effect on the next game start.
  - Entries are block ids in four forms: one block (`minecraft:rail`), a whole mod (`somemod:*`), a pattern (`*:*_fence`), or, for `never_share` only, a block tag (`#minecraft:flowers`).
  - Everything not listed still works exactly as before; the lists only take blocks out. A bad entry is reported in the log and skipped, never a crash.

## Changes
- **Blocks that fill their space no longer share it.**
  - Some blocks have no collision box but still take up their whole block, and the mod was letting them share a space as if they were flowers. That is fixed for snow layers, fire, rails, cobwebs, powder snow, string (tripwire), frogspawn, redstone dust, nether portals, vines, glow lichen, sculk veins, resin clumps, kelp, big dripleaf, and two-block plants such as tall grass, large ferns, sunflowers, lilacs, rose bushes, peonies and pitcher plants. The 1.21.5+ bushes (bush, firefly bush) are included as well, since their hit box is the full block.
  - **Crops** (wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroots, nether wart, torchflower and pitcher crops, pumpkin and melon stems, sweet berry bushes, cave vines, weeping and twisting vines, mangrove propagules) and **flowerbeds** (pink petals, wildflowers, leaf litter) no longer share either: they grow or spread to fill their own patch.
  - **Invisible technical blocks** such as the structure void are left alone.
  - All of this is decided by the block's shape and properties, not by a list of names, so other mods' blocks of the same kind behave the same way.
  - Still shareable as before: flowers, short grass, ferns, dead bushes, saplings, mushrooms, fungi, roots, sea pickles, seagrass, cactus flowers, torches, levers, buttons, bamboo, cocoa, flower pots, candles, lanterns, chains, end rods, lightning rods, fences, panes, bars, walls and gates.
- **For pack makers:** redstone dust has left the `relativeblocks:relative_placement_denied` tag, since the shape rule now covers it. Pressure plates and sugar cane remain in it.

## Good to know
- Blocks that stop sharing in this patch are only kept from being placed together from now on. Anything already sharing a space in your world stays as it is.
- Removing the mod from a world that already has orthostats or shared blocks in it shows a "Missing content" warning. Back up your world before removing any mod that adds blocks.

verfuegbar.name: Wandering Traveler
verfuegbar.changelog:
**Every title is now a single image**, which keeps more of the artwork's detail and makes titles much easier to add with a resource pack.

## Versions

- Fabric: 1.20 to 26.3
- NeoForge: 1.20.1 to 26.3
- Forge: 1.20, 1.20.1, 1.21.1 and 1.21.11

The file picks the right build for the version it is installed on. Every version and loader above was tested in game for this release.

## Titles

- Each title is drawn as one image instead of a row of font characters. They look the same as before at the GUI scales most people play on
- No title has less detail than before, and 49 of the 68 now stay sharp up to GUI scale 8, one step higher than before
- If a title's image cannot be drawn for any reason, the plain-text title shows instead and the game carries on

## Resource packs

- A title is now one PNG at `assets/wanderingtraveler/textures/title/<namespace>/<name>.png`, named after the biome or dimension id. It can be any width, and it is scaled to the same height as every other title
- Replacing one of the mod's titles and adding a title for a modded biome (from Biomes O' Plenty) were both tested in game with a separate resource pack
- Packs made for the old format, a font file plus several images per title, need converting to one image per title

Fabric API and Cloth Config are required, except on 1.20 and 1.20.1, where Cloth Config is optional. Mod Menu is optional and only adds the Config button.
